evidence.description: The `session.data(from:)` call is executed within a `Task` block that captures `self`, which is a `MainActor` isolated class. While the task is explicitly marked `@MainActor`, performing network requests on the Main Actor can block the UI thread if the underlying session implementation does not handle the threading correctly or if the data processing is heavy.

candidates.explanation: Performing network requests on the `@MainActor` can lead to UI freezes or performance degradation, as the Main Actor is intended for UI updates and light synchronization rather than heavy I/O or data processing.
candidates.title: Potential Main Thread Blocking

candidates.explanation: The `subscriptions` property is declared as a public variable, allowing external objects to modify the internal state of the `Images` class directly.
candidates.title: Public Mutable State

candidates.explanation: The code performs a linear search (O(n)) through a `Set` to find an item by URL. Since `Set` is designed for O(1) lookups via hashing, this approach negates the performance benefits of the collection type.
candidates.title: Inefficient Collection Lookup

candidates.explanation: The use of `session.getAllTasks` (which is not a standard `URLSession` method) is used to cancel tasks. If this is a custom wrapper or intended to be a standard call, it is worth noting that standard `URLSession` does not provide a simple 'cancel all' without iterating over tasks manually or managing them via a specific set.
candidates.title: Non-standard API Usage

candidates.explanation: The `items` set is updated inside an asynchronous `Task`. While the class is `@MainActor`, if multiple requests for the same URL are initiated rapidly, there is a race condition where multiple tasks could be created before the first one completes and inserts the item into the set.
candidates.title: Race Condition in Cache Update
